text:
maria: quick follow-up on standby drain/backoff behavior for cross-region failover. saw a few client timeouts during last DR exercise. TL;DR: are we comfortable with current 30s drain window + exponential backoff for lease swap? details below.
ajay: we should consider KV cache warmup — 30s might be too short for cold KV loads across regions. saw hit-rate bounce and a spike in p90s.
jordyn: agree. we observed ~120s to warm for some large contexts. could we do staged drain: soft-standby (stop new sessions) -> prewarm -> hard-swap?
maria: proposal: soft-standby = 30s, prewarm window = 90s, final cutover. backoff: 2^n * 500ms capped at 8s. thoughts?
kevin: that will increase failover time; fine if it's automated. main concern is cost (double serving during prewarm).
daphne: can we route traffic percent-based during prewarm? e.g., 10% -> 50% -> 100% to let KV fill without full duplication.
ajay: also need client-idempotency and request pinning to avoid split-brain. suggest a handshake TTL and single source-of-truth lease with short heartbeats.
sre-oncall: from oncall POV: add metrics for 'prewarm-progress' (kv-hit-rate, avg-latency, token-throughput) + alert when prewarm stalls > 3m. that would make roll decisions deterministic.
infra-bot: deploy bot: rolled out branch 'standby-prewarm-v2' to canary in us-west-2 at 2025-11-12T14:02Z :white_check_mark:
maria: here's pseudo for backoff + staged route:
``` 
// attempt lease-swap
for (i=0;i<5;i++) {
  attemptSwap()
  sleep(min(500*2^i,8000))
}
// staged traffic: 10%, 50%, 100% with 60s steps
```
jordyn: one more: data residency constraints — some tenants can't be served outside EU. prewarm must respect residency: use region-allowed flag on tenants.
daphne: @maria do we have a way to annotate tenant residency on the route policy? if not that's a blocker.
maria: we do: tenant.meta.residency = 'eu'|'global' — but routing layer needs to honor it during prewarm. i'll add to the RFC as follow-up.
ajay: ack. i'll add tests to simulate prewarm with residency enforcement (unit + e2e).
sre-oncall: if we go staged, add roll-forward cutoff: if latency/regressions > threshold during a step, rollback to previous distribution automatically.
kevin: agree. also add cost metric to rollout decision so we can abort if over budget.
maria: OK — action items: (1) add residency enforcement to routing (maria), (2) implement prewarm-progress metrics (sre-oncall), (3) staged routing + auto-rollback (ajay), (4) cost guardrails (kevin). i'll open PRs and link here.
jordyn: thanks. tl;dr: move to soft-standby + prewarm + staged cutover, residency-aware, metrics + rollback. :thumbsup:
